name: Zionism
summary: Zionism is the nationalist movement holding that Jews are a people entitled to self-determination in a state of their own in the Land of Israel. It organized Jewish immigration and settlement, revived Hebrew and Jewish national culture, and founded the State of Israel in 1948; since then it has centered on sustaining Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, encouraging immigration, and securing it militarily. Its strands range from socialist to free-market and from secular to religious, so it has little common economic program.
scope: The shared core of mainstream Zionism as set out in Herzl's The Jewish State (1896), the Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel (1948) and the World Zionist Organization's Jerusalem Program, with Jabotinsky's Iron Wall for the security doctrine common to the mainstream, and contemporary attitudes drawn from Pew's survey of Israeli Jews. Economic and social questions where Labor, General, Revisionist and Religious Zionism differ are answered as split. Separate profiles exist for strands such as Labor Zionism; Christian Zionism, post-Zionism and anti-Zionist positions are excluded.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a Zionist plank as such; inferred from Herzl's concern for workers' welfare and the Labor movement's collective institutions, though liberal strands are less committed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on wage policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Herzl promised to respect private property, but labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split.

public-ownership.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on public ownership of industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Labor Zionism was built around its labor federation, while Revisionists opposed its dominance, so adherents divide on unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Herzl called private property the basis of independence, yet the movement also made acquiring land as public national property a core task, so it is not treated as near-absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split; corporate regulation is not a Zionist question.

cut-welfare.rationale: Herzl wanted relief through work rather than charity, but the Labor strand built extensive social provision; the movement takes no common line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective settlements were a Labor Zionist hallmark, but other strands did not share the aim, so the family is split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the movement's priority on security against hostile neighbors; Zionist texts do not address surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Zionism has no position on drug policy; adherents vary with their wider politics.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Jerusalem Program commits the movement to struggle against antisemitism, and most Israeli Jews see antisemitism as common and growing; support for legal limits on hate speech is inferred from that.

strong-leader.rationale: Herzl favored an aristocratic republic, but the founding Declaration commits the state to elected authorities and mainstream Zionism defines Israel as democratic.

state-harmful.rationale: Establishing a sovereign Jewish state is the movement's central goal; Herzl called it a world need.

limit-guns.rationale: Civilian gun ownership is not a Zionist question; strands differ.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Jerusalem Program calls for encouraging army and security service, and Jabotinsky argued that settlement could only proceed behind a strong defensive force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No Zionist position; secular and religious adherents would divide.

decide-locally.rationale: Zionism is a centrally organized national project; Herzl placed leadership in a single Society of Jews and Jewish Company. Inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is outside Zionist doctrine.

traditional-family.rationale: Religious Zionists strongly uphold traditional family structures while secular adherents are more liberal, so the family is divided.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Secular and religious Zionists split sharply on marriage law; Israel has no civil marriage and the issue divides the camp.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not a Zionist question; secular and religious adherents divide.

more-religion-public.rationale: Herzl wanted clergy kept within their temples and secular Jews favor separation, while religious Zionists want the state to promote Jewish religion; the split is documented.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Zionism frames Jews as a people recovering from persecution, but takes no general position on remedying racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No Zionist position; adherents vary with their religiosity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Reviving Jewish national culture and the Hebrew language, and Jewish and Zionist education, are listed foundations of the movement.

gradual-change.rationale: Weizmann's mainstream favored incremental state-building while Revisionists demanded an immediate state, and the project itself was a radical break with diaspora life.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Encouraging Jewish immigration (aliyah) from all countries is a core plank, so adherents oppose reducing it; the commitment concerns Jewish immigration specifically.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The founding Declaration pledged cooperation with the UN, but Zionism centers national sovereignty; the answer is inferred and not stated.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is outside Zionist doctrine and divides its economic strands.

nation-first.rationale: The movement exists to represent the national interests of the Jewish people and to secure them by its own strength, rather than relying on others' goodwill.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Herzl conceived the state as neutral; Zionism takes no general position on intervening abroad.

open-borders.rationale: A Jewish state requires a Jewish majority and control over who enters, which is incompatible with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits on growth are not a Zionist question; the movement prized developing the land.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist doctrine; adherents vary.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Herzl framed the return as a feat of modern organization and technology; inferred from that developmental optimism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mainstream Zionism honors the armed struggle of the Haganah and other underground groups that helped end British rule and found the state.

experts-over-public.rationale: Herzl favored rule by a capable elite and distrusted referendums; later mainstream Zionism is democratic, so this is weak.

central-planning.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on taxation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist doctrine; strands differ.

state-directs-investment.rationale: National institutions such as Herzl's Jewish Company and later the movement's funds were designed to direct capital into settlement and development.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Strands differ between collective settlement and private enterprise.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Apart from collective settlements, mainstream Zionism assumed a money economy with respected private property.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: a state-building movement that wants national financial institutions would not abolish central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Labor movement's federation played a quasi-corporatist role, but other strands opposed it.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Declaration commits the state to elected authorities and the Jerusalem Program to a Jewish and democratic state; Zionism has always been multi-party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Herzl considered a democratic monarchy or an aristocratic republic acceptable; the movement has no monarchist program.

democracy-best.rationale: Israel is defined as Jewish and democratic, and most Israeli Jews say it can be both, though religious adherents put religious law above democracy in a conflict.

direct-votes.rationale: Herzl judged referendums an unsatisfactory procedure; mainstream Zionism is parliamentary.

workers-councils.rationale: The movement founded a parliamentary state, not a council system.

right-to-secede.rationale: Zionism is itself a claim to national self-determination, but adherents reject partition of the land where it threatens the Jewish state; no clear general position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Herzl inclined to an aristocratic republic, but later mainstream Zionism is democratic; not a settled position.

political-violence-never.rationale: Jabotinsky argued settlement needed protection by force, and mainstream Zionism honors the armed struggle that founded the state.

war-builds-character.rationale: Zionist thought treats force as necessary for defense rather than as ennobling in itself.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secular Zionists favor separating religion from government, while religious Zionists want the state to promote Jewish values; the split is documented.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Founding Zionism was secular and most Israeli Jews oppose making religious law state law, though religious Zionists favor it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: National defense by a state army is central; the program calls for service in the national army and security forces.

military-superiority.rationale: The "iron wall" doctrine holds that Jewish security depends on strength adversaries cannot overcome.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Zionism defines Jews as one people entitled to a state with a Jewish majority, while promising equal citizenship to minorities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Zionism treats the national question as primary; even Labor Zionism framed economic struggle in national terms.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Zionists regard Jews as indigenous to the Land of Israel and assert a historical right to it, while opposing competing Palestinian claims; the statement does not map onto a single answer.

civilizational-union.rationale: Zionism seeks a separate Jewish nation-state, not union with other states sharing a religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; strands range from collectivist to liberal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The program stresses mutual Jewish responsibility, pioneering, and military or national service as duties to the nation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed by mainstream Zionism; the movement valued working and developing the land.

limit-population.rationale: The movement seeks to grow the Jewish population of Israel through immigration; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Herzl envisaged a modern industrial state; the movement is developmental.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from Herzl's reliance on modern technology and organization.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist doctrine; adherents vary.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist doctrine; adherents vary.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; security priorities might cut against it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Zionism sought national restoration in the ancestral homeland but as a modern, mostly secular project; religious Zionists stress redemption more.

direct-action.rationale: Herzl sought a charter through diplomacy and the movement governed itself through elected Zionist Congresses and later the Knesset, though practical Zionism also built facts through settlement; inferred from that mix.

means-match-ends.rationale: Jabotinsky's Iron Wall argues that force must secure the Jewish state first and that peace and equal rights come after, so the means need not mirror the end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Never addressed directly, but the movement prides itself on reclaiming and farming the land and building modern towns, the opposite of a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kibbutzim rotated jobs, but the movement as a whole set out to build a full modern economy with every occupation; inferred from its nation-building aims.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Labor Zionism's kibbutzim shared by need while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement is split.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist and free-market strands disagree on the purpose of production, and the movement has no shared economic program.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Labor Zionists drew on socialist ideas of exploitation while Herzl and the Revisionists defended private property and enterprise, so the movement is split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Even socialist Zionism built its institutions through elections, and the state was founded on elected authorities; inferred from that democratic practice.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective kibbutzim and cooperative moshavim were Labor Zionism's model, but private farming and enterprise were also part of settlement, so the movement is split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Zionism explains conflict through national and security terms rather than capitalism, and its liberal strands favored commerce; inferred from its nationalist framework.

taxation-theft.rationale: Herzl's plan relied on a public body raising funds and the movement built extensive public institutions, so it treats taxes as a legitimate part of statehood; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Secular strands are broadly liberal while Religious Zionists want Jewish law to shape public life, so adherents are split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Zionism rests on the collective right of the Jewish people to self-determination, stated in the Declaration as the natural right of the Jewish people.

conscription.rationale: The Jerusalem Program lists military and national service among Zionist duties, and Jabotinsky's security doctrine depends on a citizen army.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement grounded the state in elected institutions and seeks to bring Jews in rather than treating leaving as the check on government; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Herzl used a chartered Jewish Company for practical tasks but placed political authority in a public body and the state in an elected government.

media-academia-power.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the movement's commitment to elected, democratic government as where power lies.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Declaration promises equality irrespective of race, and the mainstream defines the Jewish people by history and peoplehood rather than biology; an inference about a question it did not address.

organic-representation.rationale: Zionist institutions and Israel are organized through parties and party lists, though Herzl toyed with an aristocratic republic; inferred from that practice.

total-state.rationale: The founding Declaration guarantees freedom of religion, conscience, language, education and culture, leaving those areas outside state direction.

national-rebirth.rationale: Zionism presents itself as the renewal of a people weakened by exile, through return, Hebrew and statehood, though not as a radical purge of decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Revisionist and Religious Zionists sought the whole Land of Israel while Labor Zionists accepted partition, so the mainstream is split beyond the core homeland.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The state is built on law, a constitution-to-be and elected authorities, not personal bonds; inferred from the Declaration.

bound-labor.rationale: The Declaration promises complete social and political equality, and Herzl proposed a seven-hour working day for free workers, which excludes serfdom.

universal-morality.rationale: The Declaration bases the state on liberty, justice and peace as envisaged by the prophets of Israel and on the UN Charter, implying universal moral principles; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Zionism is a coalition of socialist, liberal, religious and revisionist strands that compete in elections, so it balances interests rather than deriving one good; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: This is the movement's founding aim, stated by Herzl and enacted in the 1948 Declaration.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Encouraging aliyah and the ingathering of exiles is a listed foundation of Zionism, and the Declaration opens the state to Jewish immigration.

revive-national-language.rationale: The revival of Hebrew was a central Zionist project and stays in the Jerusalem Program's commitment to Hebrew education.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Labor Zionism built worker-run cooperative institutions such as the Histadrut and kibbutzim, while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement is split. Inferred from the strands described in the Zionism article.

school-vouchers.rationale: Zionist programs stress Hebrew and Zionist education but do not specify how schools are funded, and Labor and free-market strands differ. Inferred from the Jerusalem Program's education aims.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Zionism has no common fiscal doctrine; Labor and General Zionists differed on state economic management and Revisionists favored private enterprise. Inferred from the economic divisions noted in the Zionism article.

economic-freedom.rationale: Herzl treated private property as a basis of independence while Labor Zionism built collective institutions and public land holding, so the movement has no common line on how economic and political freedom relate; inferred from its split economic strands.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from the movement's commitment to a state governed by law, as in the 1948 Declaration, and the Iron Wall's reliance on force and firm institutions rather than leaders' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Statehood for the Jewish people as a nation is the movement's founding principle, stated by Herzl and in the 1948 Declaration and the Jerusalem Program.

force-without-un.rationale: Jabotinsky's iron wall holds that Jewish security rests on self-reliant strength, and the 1948 Declaration pledges cooperation with the UN while the Jerusalem Program stresses defense; mainstream Zionism accepts acting alone for security, though the Declaration shows respect for the UN.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Inferred: secular Zionists are rationalist while Religious Zionists ground the project in faith and tradition, so adherents are documented as divided on religion's role.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the Jewish-state commitment to control over entry and a Jewish majority; the movement has no common welfare line, and Labor strands favored broad provision, so only a mild lean.

positive-liberty.rationale: Labor Zionism built collective social institutions while liberal and Revisionist strands stressed individual freedom, so the movement has no common view; inferred from the strands described.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Labor, General and Revisionist Zionism differed on welfare and economic policy and the movement set no common rule on work conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: Herzl's plan joined employers and workers in a common national enterprise with a short working day, and the movement prized national unity over class conflict; inferred, though Labor strands stressed worker organization.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement revived Hebrew and Jewish national culture and made Hebrew and Zionist education a foundation, so it builds on inherited culture rather than sweeping it away.

dominated-front.rationale: The Declaration pledges cooperation with the UN and the movement sought great-power backing for the state, so a common front against the Western powers runs against its approach; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Zionism organizes Jews as a nation, and its labor wing built its unions around the national project, in contrast to the internationalist Bund; inferred from its nationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Declaration guarantees equal rights irrespective of religion, race or sex, though religious Zionists favor religious law in personal status.

ban-interest.rationale: Herzl promised to respect private property and set up a Jewish Company for finance, and no Zionist program calls for banning interest; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration promises equal rights irrespective of religion, race or sex, and the Iron Wall insists on equal rights for the Arab minority.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Herzl saw the state as a national organ for the whole people, and only Labor Zionism used class analysis of it; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Zionism has no energy doctrine and strands differ; Israel’s gas development is mainstream but not a Zionist plank, so treated as split.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Jewish state’s ingathering aims at a shared Hebrew culture and language (the Jerusalem Program stresses Hebrew and Jewish culture), implying newcomers join the national culture; inferred, since Zionists differ on keeping diaspora traditions.

elite-replacement.rationale: Zionism holds that antisemitic conspiracy myths of this kind are the problem it was founded to answer, and it treats immigration (aliyah) as a deliberate national policy rather than a hidden elite plot; inferred from Herzl and the Declaration.

proportional-representation.rationale: Israel’s Knesset is elected by nationwide proportional representation, as set up under the 1948 founding framework, and the mainstream accepts it; the Declaration provides for an elected constituent assembly.

national-mission.rationale: Zionism claims self-determination for one people in its own land, not a mission to export a political system; the Declaration offers peace and cooperation to neighbors instead. Inferred from that national-particularist framing.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Labor and liberal Zionism endorse sex equality (the Declaration promises equality irrespective of sex) while Religious Zionism does not; adherents are split on whether society systematically favors men.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Mainstream Zionism built and defends Israel’s institutions and so holds its political class legitimate, though populist critics within it disagree; inferred, not a stated position.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist texts; Herzl and the Declaration stress the dignity and rights of all citizens, and Jewish religious and post-Holocaust sensibilities strongly oppose state eugenics. Inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Mainstream Zionism strongly defends Israel’s security forces and rejects external (especially international) courts judging them, in line with the Iron Wall doctrine of military self-reliance; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Herzl’s state plans welfare, labor and public works, and the Declaration promises social and political equality and development of the country, so the mainstream state has broad functions.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Zionism is a Jewish national movement, but its founding texts promise equal rights and nothing in the core program regulates marriage; mainstream Zionism is split between secular acceptance and religious opposition to intermarriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1948 Declaration promises complete equality of social and political rights to all inhabitants irrespective of religion, race or sex, and Herzl and Jabotinsky both call for equal rights for minorities.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not an issue for Zionism as such; inferred from its premise that Jews need a state of their own, which treats national self-determination as achievable in one country rather than awaiting world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents hold that Jews are an indigenous people returning to a historic homeland and so reject the colonial label, which is the central claim of their anti-Zionist critics.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Jewish-and-democratic state keeps religious courts for personal status, and Pew finds Israeli Jews favor religious law in family matters; inferred from this practice, not from the founding texts.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The mainstream core never addressed conversion law; Israel's own rules on proselytizing are contested among secular and religious Zionists, so adherents are split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a Zionist plank; inferred from the secular and liberal strands, though religious Zionists favor protecting religious norms, so adherents are split and this leans against a ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Herzl wanted clergy kept to their temples and the Jerusalem Program stresses Hebrew and Zionist education, but Israel funds religious state schools and Religious Zionists defend them; inferred from this split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a socialist doctrine, but the Iron Wall holds that a Jewish state must build a strong army while surrounded by hostile neighbors; the statement's socialist framing is not Zionism's own, so adherents are split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Declaration says the state will be founded on freedom, justice and peace and rest on elected representative bodies, and Herzl envisioned a state shaped by the people's will through referendums.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mainstream Zionism does not treat knowledge as a product of power; inferred, consistent with the audit's answer on knowledge and power.

trade-surplus.rationale: The mainstream shares no trade doctrine, since Labor, General and Revisionist Zionism differ on economics.

population-transfer.rationale: The Iron Wall rejects expulsion and the Declaration promises equal rights irrespective of religion, race or sex; some Revisionist and nationalist voices differ.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Iron Wall defends force as necessary for security and mainstream Zionism accepted armed struggle, but frames it as defense, so an absolute rule is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Labor Zionism built cooperative settlement and the mainstream does not frame progress as competition; inferred and mixed across strands.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Jerusalem Program's Jewish and democratic state implies protecting that order from parties denying it; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Zionism aims to end Jewish dependence on others' goodwill by having a state, so unused power over a people matters; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Herzl's republic and the 1948 Declaration call for elected authorities with clergy and army kept out of government; inferred separation.

vanguard-party.rationale: Herzl built a mass movement and the Declaration promises elected authorities; pioneering vanguards existed in Labor Zionism but are not a mainstream principle.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Labor Zionism prioritized workers while General and Revisionist Zionism favored markets; adherents are split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Labor Zionism favored public and national land while General and Revisionist strands favored private ownership, so the movement has no common line on selling public housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor Zionism built the Histadrut while liberal and Revisionist strands favored limits on unions; inferred as split because there is no shared Zionist position on industrial action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Herzl blamed Jewish poverty on statelessness and exclusion and proposed a Jewish Company to organize labor, not on population pressure; inferred from that analysis.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Zionism rests on a shared Jewish nationhood yet promises equal rights to all inhabitants regardless of religion or race; adherents are split on whether diversity weakens cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Herzl's state is an aristocratic republic with referendums and the 1948 Declaration provides for elected authorities; neither envisages choosing officials by lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Revisionist doctrine stresses security and force, but the Declaration pledges equal rights and a democratic state; mainstream adherents are split on suspending protections, inferred from these commitments.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Labor Zionists accepted state economic direction while General and Revisionist Zionists favored free markets, so there is no shared line on price ceilings.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Jerusalem Program defines Israel as a Jewish and democratic state and the Declaration guarantees freedom of conscience and culture, which does not fit government control of the media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Herzl wanted the army kept out of government and the Jerusalem Program frames military service as national service to the state, not to a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The Declaration and Jerusalem Program prize the ingathering of exiles and immigration, so long waits for citizenship sit badly with the movement; inferred, since they address Jewish immigrants most directly.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Labor Zionism favored egalitarian norms, while other strands did not; the movement as a whole is split.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Zionist parties range from tightly disciplined Labor and Revisionist organizations to loose coalitions, so no common view.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from Zionism's aim of Jewish sovereignty and self-determination in a state of its own, which most adherents would not pool.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Israel's Declaration sets up an elected parliamentary system, and mainstream Zionism did not call for presidential command.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Zionism is mostly secular and the Declaration provides for freedom of religion; an appointed clerical hierarchy governing a state church is not part of it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Herzl wanted priests kept in their temples, and the Declaration frames a democratic state; Pew finds most Israeli Jews are secular, though Religious Zionists differ.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Zionism is nationalist and prizes the security of the Jewish state; the Iron Wall doctrine rests on national self-defense.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Herzl wanted a state with freedom of thought and the Declaration guarantees freedom of culture; censorship for morals is split and not a Zionist plank.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed by Zionism as such; Israel has a parliamentary system without a presidency of this kind.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist sources; adherents disagree on direct-democracy tools.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Herzl called for neutrality and Jabotinsky for self-reliant strength, though the modern state depends on alliances; inferred and split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Herzl's plan kept private property, and nothing in the movement calls for banning rental housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: Israel's military is built on universal service and reserves, yet it is also a standing professional force, so adherents would not clearly endorse the statement.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agricultural settlement and the kibbutz were prized Zionist ideals, though the movement also built cities; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not a Zionist plank; Zionism concerns the Jewish people rather than other divided nations.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: Zionism had no stance against university education, and the movement valued educated founders and institutions.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Zionism makes claims about Jewish peoplehood without asserting a ranking of civilizations; not addressed.

death-penalty.rationale: Israel has used capital punishment only for exceptional crimes and Zionists are split on extending it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The 1948 Declaration guarantees equality irrespective of sex, but religious strands resist sex education, so adherents are somewhat divided.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: most Zionists are secular or modern Orthodox and do not press creationism, though religious strands do.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Religious Zionists favor restrictions while secular strands do not; adherents are split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship by descent is the basis of the Law of Return for Jews and of the movement's idea of national belonging.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Declaration promises equal rights to all inhabitants, which fits support for minority languages; inferred rather than stated.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious Zionists and secular Zionists differ on exemptions; no common view.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; the movement valued a national culture but took no stance on individual eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not a Zionist concern; inferred from Herzl's reliance on a financed Jewish Company and the mainstream's market-integrated state, which treat debts as obligations.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Labor Zionism sought to rebuild the Jewish economy through cooperatives and kibbutzim, while General and Revisionist Zionism held that statehood itself was the goal, so strands are split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1948 Declaration provided for a constitution to be adopted by an elected Constituent Assembly, which reflects the mainstream view of how a new state should be founded.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Declaration and the Jerusalem Program commit to a democratic state with equal rights, and the movement did not offer freedom as a price for development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Zionism centres on duties to the Jewish people and gives no doctrine on global aid; inferred as split between universalist and particularist strands.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the Iron Wall security doctrine and the Jerusalem Program's emphasis on Israeli military strength and self-reliance in defence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Herzl envisioned an aristocratic republic and Israel's president is chosen by the Knesset; inferred that mainstream adherents do not press for a direct vote.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Zionism has no monetary doctrine and its strands differ on economic policy, from Labor's state role to Revisionist and General free-market views.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Revisionists held the Land of Israel indivisible, whereas the 1948 Declaration accepted the UN partition and Labor strands later accepted territorial compromise, so adherents are split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from the Jerusalem Program's commitment to public land and national settlement, though Herzl and liberal strands upheld private property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Zionism has no position on classifying the USSR; Labor Zionists were socialists while others were not, and all opposed Soviet suppression of Zionism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Zionism has no environmental doctrine and its strands differ, so this is split.

collective-defense.rationale: Herzl proposed neutrality and the Iron Wall stressed self-reliance, while later Israeli governments sought great-power patrons; there is no settled stance on binding alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Mainstream Zionists reject the occupation label for the territories while accepting the principle for other cases, so adherents are split on applying it.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Herzl would keep priests in their temples and out of government, but the Jerusalem Program and Israeli practice leave the rabbinate substantial independence, so the curbing of religious property is not endorsed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the 1948 Declaration's elected parliamentary authorities and Israel's ceremonial presidency; Zionist texts do not discuss the point directly.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the Iron Wall's acceptance of force to secure the national home and the mainstream insistence on territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Herzl and the Declaration promise minorities equal rights but Zionism has no settled position on regional autonomy under a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Herzl's Jewish State is a secular aristocratic republic and the Declaration founds authority on elected bodies, with no sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Labor Zionists favoured progressive taxation and General and Revisionist Zionists favoured lighter, simpler tax, so the movement is split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from the Zionist project of creating a 'new Jew' through return to land, labor and Hebrew culture, which assumes character can be reshaped.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration commits Israel to equal rights and democratic government, and the Jerusalem Program calls for a Jewish and democratic state.

space-expansion.rationale: Zionism never addressed space; no principle points either way.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Herzl proposed an aristocratic republic that also uses referendums, an explicit blend of elite and popular elements.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from Herzl's republican model and the Declaration's elected authorities, which make leaders officeholders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Secular strands favour shared parenting while religious Zionism follows religious-court custody norms, so adherents are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Zionism is a nationalist rather than a Marxist movement and treats class conflict as secondary to national revival; inferred from its cross-class strands.

land-redistribution.rationale: Herzl accepted private property and the General and Revisionist strands favored it; land policy centered on purchase and public land for settlement, so forced redistribution is inferred as disfavored.

refugee-return.rationale: Mainstream Zionism and Israel oppose a general return of Palestinian refugees and descendants while championing Jewish return; inferred from the Jewish-majority aim, not stated in these sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Zionist claims rest on historic attachment and the Jewish people's need for a homeland, not on where co-nationals now live; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of religion and conscience and Herzl promised tolerance of all faiths, so legal punishment for leaving a religion is foreign to it.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Declaration promises equal rights irrespective of sex and Herzl wanted religion kept out of state coercion, so compulsory covering contradicts it.

common-currency.rationale: A state with its own national sovereignty and currency is the Zionist goal; supranational currency is never addressed, so inferred from its statism.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Zionism itself seeks to unite a dispersed kindred people across borders in one state (ingathering of exiles), though not framed by language family; inferred by analogy.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Zionism holds that autonomy within diaspora states does not solve the Jewish question and seeks a state of its own, though some early Zionists backed diaspora autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Herzl argued the Jewish question could only be solved by Jews leaving to found a state, and Zionism rejects the view that equal rights where Jews live is the remedy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Zionist founders appealed to will and political action rather than historical materialism; the socialist strand is the exception.

ban-cartels.rationale: Strands split between Labor Zionism with its economic concentrations and Revisionist and General Zionists favoring free enterprise; no common competition policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Labor and Revisionist strands disagree on state intervention in the economy, so the movement has no shared stance on bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Israeli Jews are divided on constraining majority decisions by courts and the Jerusalem Program speaks of a democratic state without settling it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Declaration promises equal rights regardless of sex but no quotas; mainstream Zionism does not endorse mandatory parity, inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Herzl's Jewish Company and later Zionist institutions relied on foreign capital and trade; a closed bloc is inferred as contrary to the project.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The movement has no stated trade doctrine; the Labor strand would favor such standards and the free-market strands would not.

moral-incentives.rationale: Labor Zionism's kibbutz ethos of duty contrasts with Herzl's private enterprise and the free-market strands, so adherents are split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Iron Wall defends armed force for security and Revisionists ran armed underground groups, but mainstream Zionism built institutions first; a vanguard creating revolution is inferred as not central.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Herzl's aristocratic republic was based on merit rather than birth and the Declaration promises equal rights; inferred from this.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Zionism is a movement of national revival centred on Jewish history and Hebrew culture, so history taught from the nation's own story fits; inferred rather than stated.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Zionism claims self-determination for Jews and Jabotinsky treated the Arabs as a people with its own national claims, so rule over others as tutelage is not a Zionist doctrine; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: A state built on national revival, with a Declaration appealing to national solidarity, would favour teaching loyalty to the state and its symbols; inferred, not documented.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Declaration promises equality irrespective of race but Zionism has no program on admissions or hiring preferences, and adherents are split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Zionist strands from socialist to free-market have no common monetary doctrine; Herzl proposed a chartered company and banks, not public money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Herzl kept private property and the mainstream is not Marxist, so collapse theory is not part of the core; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Zionism has no predecessor empire in the sense meant, and the movement has no stated doctrine on influence over former imperial lands; split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Herzl's plan and the state's later practice rest on trade, capital and diaspora finance from the world economy, so delinking is not a Zionist aim; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The labor-aristocracy thesis is a Marxist-Leninist doctrine that mainstream Zionism does not hold; inferred from its non-Marxist core.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Declaration pledges full social and political equality irrespective of religion, race or sex, which sits against a right to discriminate on any grounds.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Declaration promised a constitution guaranteeing equality and freedoms, though Israel never adopted one entrenched document and adherents differ; inferred support.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Zionism relied on the Balfour Declaration and Mandate and Israel's borders on armistice lines, so voiding such arrangements is unlikely to be accepted; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Declaration provides for elected authorities and Herzl proposed an aristocratic republic rather than hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Herzl's state is governed by majority decision, with referendums; minorities are protected by equal rights.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from Herzl's constitutional republic and the Declaration's democratic principles.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Declaration set up an elected Constituent Assembly and Herzl chose a republic over a monarchy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from broad Israeli support for animal welfare; not a Zionist doctrine.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from Jewish law on humane slaughter and Israeli animal-welfare norms.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from Herzl's concern for workers' welfare and the movement's collective institutions.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Zionism is an organised political project of immigration, settlement and service in the state.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not a Zionist theme; inferred that the nationalist movement does not endorse this critique.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; strands split but the mainstream does not adopt this theory, inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal and Labor strands, which accept the world economy and integration.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Declaration guarantees equal political rights to all inhabitants irrespective of religion, race or sex.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the national self-determination principle against external direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Split: Labor Zionism stressed self-reliance while the state depends on diaspora and foreign support.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Split: Revisionist and Religious Zionism claim the historic homeland while others accept compromise.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Zionism holds Jews are the indigenous people of Israel and the Declaration gives equal rights to all inhabitants.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Declaration grounds the state in the Holocaust and the struggle against Nazi Germany; inferred for constitutions generally.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on the uniqueness of the Nazi genocide, though anti-communist strands exist.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; inferred acceptance of the mainstream historical view.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common position.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no common position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's equal rights for the sexes, with no explicit stance on this claim.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Herzl modelled the state on European institutions and described it as an outpost of civilization; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Herzl kept the army in barracks and out of government, and the Declaration calls for elected civil authorities.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist sources; Labor and liberal strands differ.

filial-duty.rationale: Not a Zionist plank as such; inferred from the Jewish tradition of honouring parents that the movement's mainstream shares.

office-by-exam.rationale: Herzl and the 1948 Declaration put government in the hands of elected authorities, not an examination-selected class.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Strands differ: socialist and statist Zionists favour control of key industries, liberal and Revisionist ones favour open markets; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Split: secular Zionists favour easy divorce while religious Zionists accept rabbinic control of marriage; Pew shows Israeli Jews divided over religious law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Herzl and the Declaration envisage ordinary representative government with elected authorities, not binding mandates with instant recall.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Labor and General Zionists differ on social insurance and market solutions; the movement has no common pension doctrine.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Jerusalem Program stresses public land and Jewish settlement, and most Israeli land is held nationally and leased; Herzl however allowed private property, so this is inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: A democratic Jewish state with elected authorities, as in the Declaration and Herzl, implies a legislature controlling the public purse.

single-official-language.rationale: Hebrew revival is central, but Herzl pictured many languages kept in the Jewish state and the Declaration guarantees equal rights; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the Zionist project itself relied on purchasing land, and Israel lets non-citizens own some property; a blanket ban is not a Zionist plank.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The Declaration promises equal rights irrespective of religion, race or sex, a formal equality, not judgment by outcomes; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Split: Labor Zionism prized simple labor and kibbutz austerity while Herzl and liberal strands accepted market economy.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: No doctrine; Israel has at times aided foreign groups, but the Iron Wall security doctrine concerns defence of Israel itself.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's commitment to cooperate with the UN and Herzl's stress on neutrality.

corporate-influence.rationale: Zionist strands range from socialist to free-market, so the movement has no common line on business lobbying; inferred as split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Mainstream Zionists back state sovereignty but are split on restricting foreign-funded NGOs; inferred from the movement's divided contemporary politics.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Jewish state's demographic aim leans on aliyah rather than birth incentives, and adherents differ on family policy; inferred as split.

residents-only-property.rationale: Public land held for the nation is a Jerusalem Program theme, but restricting purchases to local residents is not a Zionist plank; inferred as split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Herzl planned shorter hours and public works through the Jewish Company, but Labor and General Zionists disagree on guaranteed work; inferred as split.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Declaration pledges peace and good neighbourliness with a democratic state, so the idea fits, though it is not a stated doctrine; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Herzl and the Declaration build a state on law and elected authorities, so a general duty to obey law fits better than not; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Zionism relied on international recognition such as the UN partition and the Declaration appeals to the UN, so it does not hold absolute non-intervention; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Labor Zionism built industry-wide union structures while Revisionists and General Zionists opposed them; the strands split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Zionism arose as a response to antisemitism, including conspiracy myths, and the Jerusalem Program commits to fighting it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage in Israel is run through religious authorities and mainstream adherents keep the institution; inferred from the Pew survey and the movement's family-centred nationalism.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Declaration promises a democratic state with elected authorities and equal rights, which fits open government; right of access itself is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Early agricultural settlement was local in character, but Zionism has no program on local production; inferred as split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Zionism organized through the Zionist Congress and the World Zionist Organization, permanent formal bodies, rather than small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Adherents back sovereignty but the Declaration and the movement also sought UN and international recognition; inferred as split.

religious-nation.rationale: Religious Zionists tie the nation to Judaism while secular strands define it as a people with a shared culture and language; Pew shows Israeli Jews divided.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Declaration claims a place among the family of nations as an equal, so Zionism rejects ritual deference to a leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from Zionism's national project of pooling resources for settlement and state-building rather than regional retention; not addressed directly.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: strands range from socialist to free-market, but the movement as a whole does not make common ownership of productive property a goal.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not a Zionist concern as such; Israel allied with both blocs at different times and adherents differ.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from Israel's mixed system of public funding with sick funds and private providers, not from a stated Zionist principle.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religious and traditional Zionists, a large share of adherents, reject this view, and Pew finds Israeli Jews divided on religion's role; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Zionist strands split between socialist and free-market views, so there is no common answer.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Declaration promises equal social and political rights regardless of sex, which implies equality through law and not economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Not a Zionist aim; the socialist strand's collective child-care was not adopted by the wider movement, so inferred as mildly opposed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Hebrew revival was central, but the movement coined and adopted words rather than demanding a purge of loanwords; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: The mainstream sources do not address treaties with internal nations; inferred as split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Zionism aims at a nation-state, though it built kibbutzim; communal living was one strand's method and not the model for society.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement of Jews in the Galilee and Negev, where Arabs or few Jews lived, was long state policy; contested among adherents and inferred from that record.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Strands range from socialist to free-market, and the movement offers no common third-way doctrine; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Zionism grounds its claim in the Jewish people's historical and religious tie to the Land of Israel, which the Declaration says shaped their identity there; Wikipedia reports advocates held this right outweighed the claim of the existing Arab population, though many adherents also stress other grounds such as need for refuge.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Declaration cites the massacre of millions of Jews in Europe as proof of the urgency of a Jewish state, so denial contradicts a founding premise of the state.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Zionist founding texts never address it; inferred from the Declaration's promise of freedom of conscience and equal rights and from Israeli mainstream practice, with some Religious Zionists dissenting.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Declaration provides for elected authorities and a Constituent Assembly, and Herzl placed Zionist policy under free public opinion, so suppressing opposition conflicts with the movement's democratic framing.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of religion and conscience, and Herzl's state keeps clergy to their temples; Religious Zionists favour more religious law, so this is not stronger than -1.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Zionism presents itself as national self-determination for a people, not rule of overseas territory for a ruling country; inferred from that framing, since critics dispute the description.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The issue is a Muslim religious duty that Zionist sources never address; inferred that adherents would reject a doctrine of obligatory armed resistance directed against Jewish statehood.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Herzl keeps clergy out of government and the Declaration sets up an elected state, so mainstream Zionists reject removing rulers by force for not following religious law; Religious Zionism is a partial exception.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Herzl proposed an aristocratic republic with referendums while Labor Zionism built kibbutz-style direct democracy, so adherents are split and the sources do not settle it.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Zionism is a national movement organised around Jewish peoplehood rather than around overlapping race, sex and class analysis; inferred from that focus and not discussed in the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The sources never address it; liberal and secular Zionists would agree and Religious Zionists would disagree, so adherents are split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist texts; secular strands lean toward allowing it while Religious Zionism opposes it, so adherents are genuinely divided.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The mainstream Zionist family has long contained distinct Labor, Liberal and Revisionist strands that define themselves on a left-right axis, so adherents would not call it obsolete; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Labor Zionism took this from Marxism while General and Revisionist Zionists did not; the movement as a whole is split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The 1948 Declaration offers peace and equal citizenship to neighbors regardless of religion; the Western-values framing is not Zionist, so this is inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Declaration grounds the state in the people's right and a UN resolution and ensures freedom of religion, though it invokes the 'Rock of Israel'; religious strands dissent.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Israeli Jews are divided between secular and religious views of public religious expression, and the sources show no unified Zionist position.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not a Zionist concern; inferred from the Declaration's commitment to equality of social and political rights regardless of sex.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Declaration promises the state will foster development for all inhabitants and social equality; the strands differ on how far, so this is a mild lean.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Iron Wall doctrine rests on military strength and the Declaration calls on the new state to defend itself against attack.

rich-first.rationale: Not a Zionist plank, and the Labor and market-oriented strands differ on inequality; split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Iron Wall holds that the Jewish settlement needs the protection of a great power, which implies alignment instead of neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Herzl proposed an aristocratic republic and the 1948 Declaration set up elected authorities, so hereditary succession of the leader is rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Zionist strands differ on economics, from the cooperative Labor tradition to free-market General Zionism; no common position.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; Israeli governments across strands have differed on lender conditions, so split.

property-franchise.rationale: The Declaration promises equal political rights irrespective of religion, race or sex, and Herzl's state had referendums; no property qualification is part of the program.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a Zionist concern; inferred from the movement's modernist, humanist framing of national revival with no link to ecofeminism.

reification.rationale: Marxist reification theory is foreign to mainstream Zionism, which favors private property and market economy in most strands; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mainstream Zionism, including Herzl, accepted private ownership of the press and the Declaration guarantees freedom of conscience; inferred that formal freedoms are held to be real.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Herzl's state is governed by law and the Declaration pledges a democratic state with elected authorities, and the Jerusalem Program calls it Jewish and democratic.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Declaration guarantees full political equality irrespective of religion, race or sex, and Jabotinsky's Iron Wall insists on equal rights, so a racial vote limit is rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Herzl envisaged referendums and direct consultation; inferred that online participation fits, though the sources do not discuss the internet.

open-government-data.rationale: The Declaration and Jerusalem Program stress a democratic state; inferred that open records fit, though not stated.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious Zionists favor religious marriage law while secular strands want civil marriage; adherents are split.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Herzl calls for tolerance of other faiths and the Declaration ensures equal rights, so boycotts of a religious minority's shops are not a Zionist position.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not a Zionist concern; inferred from the shared commitment to a democratic Israel, while the strands differ on how far to go beyond elected institutions.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Zionists are split between secular and religious strands, so there is no shared view on updating religious law; inferred from the divide described in the Pew survey.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Labor, General and Revisionist Zionists differ on economics, so adherents are split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Israeli military has allowed openly gay service since 1993 and mainstream Israeli opinion accepts it, but religious Zionists dissent.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of religion and conscience and Herzl wanted faith kept in its place; no strand wants a state atheism campaign.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the Iron Wall security doctrine and the state's emphasis on security institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: the movement seeks a Jewish-majority state with equal individual rights, not communal power sharing, and it rejected binationalism.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from Herzl's Jewish Company and the Labor and state-building tradition that relied on organised national institutions over charity.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents are split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the representative parliamentary model in the Declaration, with no support for delegable voting.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents are split: Reform and secular Zionists agree, while religious Zionists follow Orthodox practice.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Declaration guarantees equality of social and political rights irrespective of sex, which the mainstream reads as equal standing within marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Israeli law reserves the national vote to citizens, though the Declaration promises equal rights and residents' voting is debated; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Zionist strands range from Labor to free-market and have no common program on rent; split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Zionism has no plank on abolishing copyright and Israel's economy, a start-up economy, relies on patents; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Zionist youth movements and the Gadna and army pre-service programmes train youth for national service, though not all strands do; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Israel is understood to hold nuclear weapons on its own territory for security, and the doctrine of the Iron Wall rests on strength; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Mainstream Zionism values sovereignty and security alliances such as the US one, and has hosted few foreign bases; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The Declaration of Independence cites the Nazi Holocaust as a cause for the state, and Holocaust recognition is central to Zionist memory and state practice.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Labor Zionism's collective economy and liberal and Revisionist Zionism's markets pull in opposite ways; split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Iron Wall says defence by force is necessary and moral, and the Declaration states the right of self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Declaration and Zionist writing root the nation in its ancient homeland and unbroken connection to it through the diaspora.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Mainstream Zionism, a nationalist and often religious movement, treats sex as biological; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and Israeli society holds varied views; split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Israel honours the fallen with state memorial days and the Holocaust dead as martyrs (kedoshim), though religious and secular strands honour them differently; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Zionism is a national and largely secular political movement framing politics as about interests and statehood; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Jerusalem Program and Herzl call for the ingathering of Jews (aliyah) to the state, not a homeland that merely inspires the diaspora, though cultural Zionism held otherwise.

culture-before-state.rationale: Herzl's political Zionism puts the state first, though Ahad Ha'am's cultural Zionism differed, and the Jerusalem Program says both matter.

god-not-male.rationale: Orthodox Zionists keep traditional language and secular ones are indifferent; split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Most Zionists, religious and secular, treat texts as authoritative or as heritage and not as judged by feminism; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Declaration promises equal rights to all inhabitants, though 'Jewish labour' was a Labor Zionist aim; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Zionism does not call for merging regions by people; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Histadrut-style unions tied to a ruling party and independent unions both exist within Zionism, so the movement has no common line; inferred from the strands described.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Labor Zionists held this view while General and Revisionist Zionists did not, so the movement as a whole is split.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Zionism has no common economic program; socialist strands favoured public provision and free-market strands did not.

second-chamber.rationale: Israel's Knesset is a single chamber and the Declaration envisages one elected assembly; mainstream Zionism shows no push for a second chamber, inferred from these.

municipal-property.rationale: Zionist land and enterprise policy centred on national and cooperative bodies and private owners, not municipal ownership; inferred from the movement's national focus.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Herzl's Jewish State envisages a single national state; a confederation of self-governing towns is not part of the program, inferred from that.

family-wage.rationale: Family wages are not a Zionist plank; Labor strands might favour it and free-market strands not, so adherents are split.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's economic strands differ on regulation, so no common position can be inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by Zionism's founding texts; no shared position can be inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; the security-minded mainstream and its liberal wing would likely differ, so the answer is split.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' views on privacy versus security differ and nothing in the sources settles it.

person-over-state.rationale: The Declaration guarantees equal social and political rights and freedom of conscience to all inhabitants, which fits treating persons as ends; inferred, as Zionism is also collectively focused.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Secular and religious Zionists differ, and Pew finds Israeli Jews divided between secular, traditional and religious identity.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Israel is a unitary state with a single sovereign legislature, so inferring that regional powers would rest on the Knesset's authority is natural; the sources do not discuss it.

gm-crops.rationale: Not a Zionist issue; no shared position can be inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; Zionism built both agricultural settlements and cities, so no position follows.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Zionism defines Jews as a nation entitled to self-determination, not as a race, and the Declaration bases the state on equal rights; inferred from that national framing.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Jewish peoplehood and heritage is central to Zionism and the Jerusalem Program's emphasis on Jewish identity and culture; read as pride in ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Jabotinsky's Iron Wall casts force as defensive, but Israeli mainstream doctrine also accepts preventive strikes, so adherents are split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Herzl held that Jews are a people by shared history and fate, not language, and the Declaration grounds peoplehood in history and the Bible; Hebrew was revived later.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Declaration promises equal political rights to all inhabitants irrespective of religion, and Israel elects the Knesset from a single common electorate.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Mainstream Zionism accepted partition in 1947 and sees threats from hostile neighbors rather than foreign plots to break the country up; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Not a shared Zionist plank; Labor strands favor public provision and liberal and Revisionist strands favor fees, so adherents are split.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed by the core of the movement; strands differ and no common position exists.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the movement's emphasis on land reclamation and afforestation and its aim of a lasting home for coming generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The Declaration pledges equality of social and political rights irrespective of sex, which fits equal treatment rather than weighting women's values; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Jabotinsky's Iron Wall doctrine, common to the mainstream, rests Israel's security on overwhelming strength, so unilateral minimal armament is rejected.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; Herzl himself pursued confidential diplomacy with the Sultan and the powers, and Israeli governments have kept secret talks.

capital-controls.rationale: Not a shared Zionist plank; Labor-era Israel used currency controls while later liberal strands liberalised capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The 1948 Declaration set up a state with its own armed forces, and the Iron Wall doctrine rests on a strong state-controlled military; the mainstream accepted the disbanding of the pre-state militias.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Mainstream Zionism treats the army's defence of Israel as a duty, and the Iron Wall doctrine holds that security rests on military strength.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labor Zionism built the Histadrut and its collective agreements while Revisionists favoured market contracts, so strands are split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Labor and General Zionists differ on welfare and Revisionists favour lower taxes, so the shared core has no position.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Strands differ on economic policy and the core documents set no fiscal rules, so adherents are split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not a Zionist concern; strands differ and the core documents do not address it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Zionism built and took over state institutions at independence rather than smashing them, though it did so by its own revolt against Mandate rule; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Zionist strands ran from kibbutz socialism to free-market liberalism, so adherents are split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the core documents; strands differ.

sacred-nation.rationale: Zionism treats the Jewish nation as a lasting community with a historic bond to the land, and the Declaration invokes it in terms of eternal ties and national revival.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; strands differ on welfare.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Zionism asserts national unity and does not treat the centre as colonising its own regions; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Herzl and the Declaration appeal to universal human equality and rights, which fits a shared human nature, but the statement is not discussed; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: The Declaration promises freedom of conscience and equal social and political rights, and Israel has long had a public broadcaster, but the independence point is inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Zionism is mostly secular and religiously mixed, so it takes no common view on whether religions share one truth; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Labor Zionism favoured cooperative farming and state support while liberal and Revisionist strands favoured markets, so adherents are split.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not a founding text issue; inferred from the security doctrine of the Iron Wall and Israel's mainstream policy of retaining deterrence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Labor Zionists favoured workers' parties while General and Revisionist Zionists did not, so the movement is split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Declaration's equal rights irrespective of sex.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Declaration promises complete equality of social and political rights irrespective of religion, race or sex, which implies equal property rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not a Zionist question; Hebrew revival is central but naming of regional varieties is not addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Herzl's plans for state and company planning and the modern Israeli reliance on regulation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Herzl wants clergy kept to their temples and out of government, and the Declaration provides for elected authorities, so no formal role for traditional leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed by the shared core; strands differ on state limits on liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No documented position; mainstream Zionism did not address sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Hebrew revival and Hebrew education are core Zionist goals, so expecting immigrants to learn Hebrew fits; a legal requirement is inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Zionism has no common labor program: Labor Zionism built the Histadrut while Revisionist and General Zionists favored free enterprise.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by the founding documents; Israel's practice of identity-card voting is not a Zionist plank, so adherents are not split on principle.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Declaration promises freedom of conscience and religion yet Israel keeps an Orthodox rabbinate with legal authority over marriage; Pew shows Israeli Jews divided on religion's role.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The mainstream holds that Israel must be both Jewish and democratic, so adherents tie democracy to more than procedure but not to one fixed view.

premarital-sex.rationale: The mainstream is largely secular and Israeli Jewish society is permissive on this; religious Zionists dissent, so inferred and contested.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist sources; inferred from the Declaration's commitment to freedom and Israel's democratic self-image.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Zionism's economic strands (socialist, General, Revisionist) differ, so adherents are split on replacing welfare with a cash scheme.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Declaration of Independence guarantees complete equality of social and political rights irrespective of religion, race or sex, and Herzl's The Jewish State envisaged women voting.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The mainstream secular majority is critical of rabbinic control of marriage, but religious Zionists reject the claim; inferred from the split in Pew's survey.

race-social-construct.rationale: Zionism defines Jews as a people, with strands that stress ancestry and others culture; adherents are split and the sources do not address race as a category.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Israel has an Authority for the Advancement of the Status of Women and the Declaration promises equal rights regardless of sex; inferred as accepted by the mainstream.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Split: Labor Zionism put land in national ownership through the Jewish National Fund, while liberal strands favour private claims.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the contemporary mainstream Israeli view that international courts lack jurisdiction over Israel's leaders.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Split: religious Zionism reads scripture as binding, while the secular majority of Israeli Jews does not.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The Declaration of 1948 pledges complete equality of social and political rights to all inhabitants irrespective of sex.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: Zionism has no common economic programme and no planned-state doctrine to defend.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's call for democratic elections to a constituent assembly and Israel's directly elected Knesset.

national-church-status.rationale: Split: religious Zionists want state backing for Orthodox institutions, while many secular Israeli Jews object.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the Declaration offers Arab inhabitants equal citizenship, not territorial autonomy, and mainstream Zionism has not backed it.
